newsitem.title: USA: Talks on California redwoods adjourn to Friday.
newsitem.headline: Talks on California redwoods adjourn to Friday.

text.p: Government and timber company negotiators racing a deadline to prevent logging of thousands of acres of ancient northern California redwoods met for 5 1/2 hours Thursday, then adjourned until morning.

In the face of a timber company deadline that could permit cutting to begin as soon as Monday, talks were to resume at 8:30 a.m. EDT (1230 GMT) Friday in the office of Sen. Dianne Feinstein. No statement was issued by negotiators.

The California Democrat met with Deputy Interior Secretary John Garamendi, California State Resources Secretary Doug Wheeler and Charles Hurwitz, the Texas financier who heads MAXXAM Inc., which owns the land in rural Humboldt County.

Pacific Lumber Co., a unit of MAXXAM, agreed to delay the start of logging for two weeks in the virgin 3,000-acre (1,200-hectare) Headwaters area, a small part of the nearly 200,000 acres (81,000 hectares) owned by the company.

If no agreement is reached, logging could begin Monday on the nation's largest privately held tract of redwoods. Environmentalists have sought to have 60,000 acres (24,000 hectares) protected, saying the area is an ecosystem necessary to preserve endangered fish and birds.
But the negotiations centre on the Headwaters area, a buffer zone of 1,500 acres (600 hectares) and about 1,800 to 3,000 acres (700-1,200 hectares) included in five other forest parcels.

The other virgin groves are the 480-acre Allan Creek Grove, including the 50-foot Allan Creek Falls; the 400-acre Owl Creek Grove; the 280-acre Shaw Creek Grove; the 400-acre All Species Grove and the 300-acre Elkhead Springs Grove, according to Doug Thron, a wilderness guide and photographer who has visited and photographed the area extensively. Maxxam had no precise figures on the groves.
Buffer zones that have been partially logged would expand the 1,860 acres in the groves, he said.
By contrast, the Muir Woods National Monument of redwoods near San Francisco is 560 acres.
The struggle between environmentalists and the company sparked one of the largest one-day mass arrests ever in California this month when 897 people were arrested.
